findings.why_not_priced: The reimbursement amount was never disclosed and the stock trades at a discount the treasury does not explain: bitcoin alone is about 63% of market cap, before $1.8bn of corporate debt. No sell-side note found mentions a buyback, and if one were expected the stock would not have fallen 25% in a week on no company news. It is inference, not a company statement, so it is sized small with a wide upper tail.

The 885 MW Texas exclusivity with the Sandersville tenant began 2026-07-14 (CEO: 'an exclusivity window, not at the finish line', with industry windows of 30-120 days), so it is now about 133 days old. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Texas election news drove -11% and -17% on 11-04/05. The Sandersville lease announcement (2026-07-14) was a positive catalyst before the FQ3 print. No reaction to an exclusivity update on a call is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: The election shock is priced. What may not be priced is that a call with no Texas signing, or with an exclusivity that is extended or quietly lapsed, removes the near-term catalyst the remaining holders are waiting for. If the market already assumed no lease before December, the stock would not have kept selling off into the print. Both tails are real, because a signing would be a large positive, so the range is wide.
